# Refactor: decompose `src/commands/interview.ts` god class

**File:** `src/commands/interview.ts` — 1,630 lines, 41 exports, 9 logical sections.

## Problem statement

`src/commands/interview.ts` carries the whole `wl interview` backend — clarifying-section
detection, Q/A parsing and lossless re-serialisation, the producer-review explanation
(LLM + structured fallback), LLM-assisted question extraction, the interactive walkthrough
loop, readline plumbing and Commander registration — in one 1,630-line module. It breaches
the 1,000-line maintainability ceiling adopted for WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7, so navigating,
reviewing and safely changing any one concern means holding the whole file in view.

## Users

- **Agents implementing interview/LLM changes** — need one concern (e.g. the answer
  re-serialiser, or the extraction prompt) locatable by file search instead of by reading
  1,630 lines; a monolith inflates context cost and increases the chance of editing the
  wrong helper with a similar name (`cleanQuestion` vs `firstLine` vs `truncateBytes`).
- **Reviewers/auditors** — need a diff whose blast radius is legible from the touched
  module boundary.
- **Producers running `wl interview`** — benefit indirectly: behaviour-preserving
  decomposition lowers the regression risk of every future change to the command.

Example user stories:

- As an agent fixing a Q/A parsing defect, I want the parser and re-serialiser in one
  focused module, so that I can reason about round-trip losslessness without loading the
  LLM and Commander code.
- As a reviewer, I want each extracted module to state one responsibility, so that I can
  judge a diff against a single boundary.
- As a maintainer, I want the `wl interview` command behaviour and the public module
  surface unchanged, so that no test, registry entry or documented flag needs reworking.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Ceiling met.** `src/commands/interview.ts` and every file under `src/interview/` is
   ≤ 1,000 lines (target: largest extracted module ≤ 500). Evidence recorded in the work
   item as `wc -l` output for the module family.
2. **Public surface unchanged.** All 41 current exports of `src/commands/interview.ts`
   (2 section, 4 Q/A, 15 explanation, 11 extraction, 5 loop, 4 registration) plus the
   default `register` export remain importable from the unchanged specifier
   `src/commands/interview.js` with identical names, kinds and signatures; the barrel
   re-exports the full surface. `src/command-registry.ts`
   (`interview: () => import('./commands/interview.js')`) is untouched and needs no edit.
3. **Move-only, behaviour-preserving.** No logic, regex, message, ordering or flag
   changes. Test assertions, fixtures, `describe` titles and mock targets are unmodified;
   the only mechanical test change permitted is the lockstep split of the oversized suite
   `tests/cli/interview.test.ts` (1,696 lines): every resulting file is ≤ 1,000 lines,
   `describe` groups move verbatim and only import paths change. Test count is preserved
   (the split neither adds nor drops a test).
4. **No circular imports, one direction only.** Extracted modules import concrete siblings
   and `../lib/*`, `../config.js`, `../types.js`; **no** `src/interview/*` module imports
   the `src/commands/interview.ts` barrel. The dependency direction is
   `commands/interview.ts` → `interview/*`.
5. **Responsibilities documented.** Every new module carries a one-line module doc comment
   naming its single responsibility, and existing provenance comments/work-item ids
   (`WL-0MU55UDBJ008DJ67`, `WL-0MUUAMP7M008Z4GK`, `WL-0MUH7ACKJ0024VGF`,
   `WL-0MUX2W8IN005RW66`, `WL-0MUQ0VP800068DNX`) move with their code.
6. **Builds and tests.** `npm run build` (tsc, NodeNext, `rootDir: src`) is green and the
   full project test suite passes via `/skill:test`.
7. **Documentation updated.** All related documentation reflects the changes, including
   code comments, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (command/module map), `CLI.md` if any wording
   drifts, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries. `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded
   (release pipeline).

## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Relocate code and update imports only. No "while we're here" rewrites, no
  renames of public symbols, no regex or prompt-text edits. Any incidental improvement
  found en route becomes a separate `discovered-from` work item.
- **Layout: mirror `src/doctor/`.** Helpers for a single command live in a top-level
  feature directory (`src/doctor/*` ← `src/commands/doctor.ts`); this item follows that
  established precedent with `src/interview/*`. The entry file stays
  `src/commands/interview.ts` so the ESM specifier `./commands/interview.js` keeps
  resolving to `dist/commands/interview.js` under NodeNext (a directory-index barrel
  `interview/index.ts` would break that specifier).
- **No new dependencies.** Only existing imports (`../lib/llm.js`,
  `../lib/progress-feedback.js`, `../config.js`, `../mutation-lock.js`, `../types.js`,
  `../cli-types.js`, `readline`) may be used by the extracted modules.
- **No behaviour-parity tooling in scope.** A repo-wide 1,000-line guard is a separate
  open item (WL-0MVHLMKD60068VJL, `discovered-from` the sweep); this item verifies the
  ceiling with `wc -l` evidence plus a small structural assertion (see Risks).
- **Escaped backticks** only in written content; Markdown otherwise.

## Existing state

`src/commands/interview.ts` — 1,630 lines, 41 exports, single default `register`, no
module-level mutable state (only `const` regexes/constants). Section map (current `dev`):

| Lines | Section | Exports |
|---|---|---|
| 1–70 | File doc comment + imports | — |
| 71–116 | Section markers (regexes, `INSERT_WRAPPER`) | — (all private) |
| 117–160 | Section extraction | `ClarifyingSection`, `extractClarifyingSection` |
| 161–564 | Q/A parsing and re-serialisation | `ClarifyingQAPair`, `parseQAPairs`, `rebuildQAPairs`, `rebuildDescription` |
| 565–873 | Producer-review explanation | 15 (caps, context/deps types, prompt, render, fallback, LLM result) |
| 874–1052 | LLM-assisted question extraction | 11 (instruction, caps, prompt, parser, result, extract fns, section insert/merge) |
| 1053–1260 | Core interview loop | `InterviewStore`, `InterviewIO`, `InterviewOutcome`, `InterviewRunOptions`, `runInterview` |
| 1261–1291 | Interactive input | — (`createPromptLoop` private) |
| 1292–1630 | Types + command registration | `InterviewPromptLoop`, `InterviewCommandDeps`, `defaultClearPrompt`, `register` (default) |

Consumers: exactly one production importer — `src/command-registry.ts` (dynamic import,
default export only) — and one test file, `tests/cli/interview.test.ts` (1,696 lines, 19
top-level `describe` blocks, no `vi.mock`, imports 11 named exports + default). No file in
`src/`, `packages/`, `scripts/` or `bench/` imports any other symbol from the module, and
no documentation references the file path.

## Desired change

Extract cohesive modules under `src/interview/`, leaving `src/commands/interview.ts` as the
command entry (registration + interactive plumbing) **and** the public barrel. Proposed map
(export attribution is exhaustive — every current export belongs to exactly one row):

| Module | Responsibility | Exports moved | Est. lines |
|---|---|---|---|
| `src/commands/interview.ts` (entry + barrel) | Commander registration, `register` action flow, prompt loop, deps surface, re-export of the full public surface | `InterviewPromptLoop`, `InterviewCommandDeps`, `defaultClearPrompt`, `register` (default) + all re-exports | ~400 |
| `src/interview/section.ts` | Clarifying-section heading detection and extraction | `ClarifyingSection`, `extractClarifyingSection` | ~95 |
| `src/interview/qa.ts` | Q/A parsing, answer-region computation and lossless re-serialisation | `ClarifyingQAPair`, `parseQAPairs`, `rebuildQAPairs`, `rebuildDescription` | ~400 |
| `src/interview/explanation.ts` | Producer-review explanation: evidence formatting, prompt, render, structured fallback, LLM call | 15 exports | ~310 |
| `src/interview/extraction.ts` | LLM-assisted question extraction plus canonical-section insert/merge | 11 exports | ~200 |
| `src/interview/loop.ts` | Interactive walkthrough: prompt/persist answers, outcome accounting | `InterviewStore`, `InterviewIO`, `InterviewOutcome`, `InterviewRunOptions`, `runInterview` | ~220 |

Dependency direction after extraction:
`commands/interview.ts` → {section, qa, explanation, extraction, loop} →
{`../lib/llm.js`, `../lib/progress-feedback.js`, `../config.js`, `../types.js`} and
sibling modules only. `loop.ts` → `section.ts`, `qa.ts`, `extraction.ts`;
`extraction.ts` → `qa.ts`, `section.ts`. No module imports the entry barrel (AC4).

### Proposed child decomposition (structural slices)

1. **Foundation** — create `src/interview/` and extract `section.ts` + `qa.ts` (the pure,
   dependency-free parsing core). Blocks the rest.
2. **`explanation.ts`** — largest LLM cluster; independent of the loop.
3. **`extraction.ts`** — depends on `qa.ts`/`section.ts` for insert/merge helpers.
4. **`loop.ts`** — core walkthrough; depends on slices 1 and 3.
5. **Closeout** — thin the entry barrel (`src/commands/interview.ts`), lockstep split of
   `tests/cli/interview.test.ts`, module-map documentation, `wc -l` evidence, build +
   full suite.

Slices are ordered so slice 1 blocks the rest and each slice is independently move-only and
verifiable with the changed-scope test gate.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/interview.ts` — becomes entry + barrel; loses ~1,200 lines, keeps `register`
- `src/interview/section.ts` — new (heading detection/extraction)
- `src/interview/qa.ts` — new (parse/rebuild)
- `src/interview/explanation.ts` — new (producer-review explanation)
- `src/interview/extraction.ts` — new (LLM extraction + section insert/merge)
- `src/interview/loop.ts` — new (interactive walkthrough)
- `tests/cli/interview.test.ts` — split in lockstep into `tests/cli/interview/*.test.ts`
  (parsing/rebuild, loop + extraction, command integration, command `--llm`/progress,
  explanation), assertions verbatim
- `src/command-registry.ts` — read-only (specifier must keep resolving)
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — command/module map note for the new `src/interview/` modules
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `docs/design/incremental-sync.md`, `CLI.md` — read-only
  unless wording names the module layout (it does not today; verify, do not churn)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Silent behaviour drift in the re-serialiser** (the lossless round-trip is the command's
  subtle core; regexes are shared between parsing and rebuild). *Mitigation:* extract
  `qa.ts` first with zero edits, keep the 19 existing `describe` groups untouched, and land
  each slice as a separate move-only commit so a regression is bisectable.
- **Barrel/ESM resolution break.** `src/commands/interview.ts` must keep existing so
  `dist/commands/interview.js` is emitted; a `interview/index.ts` barrel would silently
  break the lazy registry. *Mitigation:* AC2 + the `lazy-command-registry` and
  `entry-point-split` suites as the oracle.
- **Circular imports** if `loop.ts` or `extraction.ts` reach back into the entry for types
  or helpers. *Mitigation:* AC4 — modules import siblings and `../lib/*` only; shared types
  live with their owning module (`section.ts`, `qa.ts`, `loop.ts`).
- **Test-file split churn.** 19 `describe` groups currently share one module scope.
  *Mitigation:* move groups verbatim; add no shared helper unless two target files need the
  same fixture, and then only a mechanical extraction.
- **Regrowth repeats.** This sweep already has a "completed" decomposition that never
  landed (see Related work). *Mitigation within scope:* documented single-responsibility
  module headers; the repo-wide guard is WL-0MVHLMKD60068VJL (separate, low priority).
- **Scope creep risk.** The split invites opportunistic "while we're here" cleanups — a
  parser rewrite, prompt-tuning, a new `--flag`, splitting the 266-line `register` action
  into sub-commands. *Mitigation:* AC3 forbids logic edits; any such opportunity is filed
  as a separate item linked `discovered-from:WL-0MVGKGXN80006V9P` rather than absorbed.
- **Review fatigue on a wide-but-shallow diff.** A move-only refactor touches many files
  for zero behavioural gain, which can invite under-review. *Mitigation:* one concern per
  commit/slice, `git diff --color-moved` for reviewers, and the unchanged suites as the
  behaviour oracle.
- **Assumption:** the 1,000-line ceiling applies to non-test source, and to a test file only
  when it is touched in lockstep with its module (sweep rule; identical to
  WL-0MVGKGHNR0019OLT AC3).
- **Assumption:** the full 41-symbol public surface is retained in the barrel rather than
  trimmed to the 12 symbols tests import. Trimming would be a breaking change for any
  external plugin consumer and buys nothing here; the barrel re-export is ~10 lines.
- **Assumption:** no consumer call-site changes are acceptable — `src/command-registry.ts`
  and the CLI help output must be byte-identical for `wl interview`.
- **Assumption:** no behavioural improvement is bundled; opportunities observed en route
  become separate `discovered-from` items.

## Related work

- WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 — parent sweep/directive: every production file > 1,000 lines is
  evaluated for decomposition (producer Q1 answered).
- WL-0MVGKGHNR0019OLT — sibling from the same sweep (`packages/shared/src/database.ts`);
  source of the lockstep test-split rule reused in AC3 and the module-map layout pattern
  (entry façade + cohesive modules + explicit dependency direction).
- WL-0MULI1N1N0001WRD — "CLI: Explanation path & new options" (completed); introduced the
  `--no-llm`/`--json` modes and the producer-review explanation path extracted here. (The
  seed description labelled this item "Interview LLM fallback"; the title above is the
  accurate one — the LLM *extraction* fallback is WL-0MUH7ACKJ0024VGF.)
- WL-0MU55UDBJ008DJ67 ("Interview replay feature"), WL-0MUUAMP7M008Z4GK ("r-i interview
  explanation does not state why an item needs producer review"), WL-0MUH7ACKJ0024VGF
  ("interview: LLM-assisted question extraction as fallback"), WL-0MUX2W8IN005RW66
  ("Feedback in interview when running LLM"), WL-0MUQ0VP800068DNX ("Interview LLM config
  schema") — all completed; provenance items for the behaviour implemented in this file,
  cited in its doc comments and moving with their code.
- WL-0MUQ0VQ8A002HHFA — "Interview LLM fallback integration" (completed); the integration
  work behind the extraction fallback path extracted here.
- WL-0MVHLMKD60068VJL — proposed repo-wide file-size guard (`discovered-from` the sweep);
  the reason this item's ceiling check is manual plus a small structural assertion.
- WL-0MVGKH6Z1000XWGJ, WL-0MVGKH9Z900178UF, WL-0MVGKH47T007GKN1, WL-0MVGKHCP9005SJPZ,
  WL-0MVGKHFT4003X6JW — companion god-class items from the same sweep (`init.ts`,
  `github-sync.ts`, `fetcher.ts`, `dispatcher-anchor.ts`, `downtime-log.ts`).
- Repo precedent for layout: `src/doctor/*` helper modules consumed by
  `src/commands/doctor.ts`.

## Appendix: decision log (agent-proposed; producer may override)

No producer interview questions were required: the seed context (goal, drafted ACs, parent
directive) plus two completed sibling intakes from the same sweep answer every open choice,
and all decisions below are reversible at plan/implement time. Recorded for review.

- **Q: Where should the extracted modules live?**
  **Recommended and chosen: `src/interview/`, mirroring the existing `src/doctor/`
  precedent** (top-level feature directory consumed by one command module). The entry stays
  `src/commands/interview.ts` so the ESM specifier `./commands/interview.js` keeps
  resolving under NodeNext.
  Alternatives considered: (b) flat siblings `src/commands/interview-*.ts` (works, but mixes
  six command-specific helpers into the already crowded flat `src/commands/` namespace);
  (c) a `src/commands/interview/index.ts` barrel (breaks the emitted
  `dist/commands/interview.js` specifier the lazy registry depends on).

- **Q: How granular should the split be?**
  **Recommended and chosen:** five extracted modules plus the entry (map above), one per
  existing section banner, each 95–400 lines — comfortably under the ceiling without
  inventing new boundaries mid-move.
  Alternatives considered: a two-way split (parsing vs everything else ≈ 470 / 1,150 lines —
  fails AC1); eight-plus micro-modules (churn without benefit).

- **Q: Keep the full 41-symbol barrel, or trim to the 12 symbols tests import?**
  **Recommended and chosen: keep the full surface.** The parent epic's "used symbols only"
  barrel decision (WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 Q2) applied to a module where unused symbols were
  genuinely internal; here every symbol is a documented part of this command module's
  surface and trimming risks breaking out-of-repo plugin imports for ~10 lines of saved
  barrel. Behaviour-parity is the priority (AC2).

- **Q: Split the oversized test suite in this item?**
  **Recommended and chosen: yes, mechanical lockstep split only.** `tests/cli/interview.test.ts`
  (1,696 lines) exceeds the same ceiling, and the parent sweep rule evaluates test files in
  lockstep with their module (identical to WL-0MVGKGHNR0019OLT AC3). Assertions, fixtures and
  `describe` titles are unchanged; only file location and import paths move.

- **Q: Add a file-size regression guard here?**
  **Recommended and chosen: no — out of scope.** A guard is repo-wide policy
  (WL-0MVHLMKD60068VJL) affecting every sibling god-class item. This item records `wc -l`
  evidence and (optionally, if cheap) a structural assertion that the interview module
  family stays ≤ 1,000 lines; the repo-wide gate stays a separate item.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MQDR51JO0037ISJ** – Eliminate unsafe as any casts in shortcut dispatch (detail view and duck-typing) (completed)
- **WL-0MQDR5ICN0098ID6** – Remove unused WorkItem import from index.ts (completed)
- **WL-0MUQ0VQ8A002HHFA** – Interview LLM fallback integration (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: absorbed, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+387 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, accounting (+361 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: 0mu55udbj008dj67, ac2, action, add, adds (+335 more)

# Decompose the `src/commands/doctor.ts` god class

**File:** `src/commands/doctor.ts` (1,658 lines at intake time; 1,582 when the item was created)

## Problem statement

`src/commands/doctor.ts` is a single 1,658-line module that carries the entire
`wl doctor` CLI surface: six module-level notice/formatting helpers at the top
and eleven command registrations (root `doctor` validation, `upgrade`,
`stage-sync`, `prune`, `cache`, `foreign-items`, `audit-gaps`,
`dangling-parents`, `priority`, `file-paths`, `migrate`), each with its own
inline `async` action body. The `--fix` interactive flow and the findings
aggregation of the root command alone occupy ~385 lines inside one nested
callback. Navigating, reviewing or changing one subcommand requires holding the
other ten in view, so every doctor change carries avoidable regression risk and
the file sits above the 1,000-line maintainability ceiling adopted for
WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7.

## Users

- **CLI maintainers (agents and humans)** need to change one doctor subcommand
  (e.g. `prune`, `file-paths`, the `--fix` prompt) without reasoning about
  1,600 unrelated lines.
- **Reviewers/auditors** need a diff attributable to a single subcommand so the
  blast radius of a change is legible.
- **Future agents implementing doctor work items** (e.g. the open
  WL-0MVM8V79C003XH2J `wl doctor prefix` item) need a named, findable module
  per subcommand instead of appending to a monolith.

Example user stories:

- As an agent adding a new doctor subcommand, I want an existing per-subcommand
  module template so that registration is mechanical and reviewable.
- As a reviewer, I want a `prune` change to touch only the prune module and its
  tests so that I can verify it against its own suite.
- As a maintainer, I want every doctor file under 1,000 lines so that it is
  readable in a single pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No file exceeds 1,000 lines.** After the change, `wc -l` reports ≤1,000 for
   `src/commands/doctor.ts` (now a thin registrar) and for every module created
   by the split.
2. **Public entry point unchanged.** `src/commands/doctor.ts` still provides
   `export default function register(ctx: PluginContext): void`, so
   `src/command-registry.ts` (`doctor: () => import('./commands/doctor.js')`)
   and every existing CLI test import path keep working with **no importer
   edits**.
3. **Behaviour-preserving, move-only refactor.** No change to subcommand names,
   flags, help text, human output strings, JSON payload shapes or exit codes; no
   existing test file is modified (import paths, fixtures or assertions), and
   all existing `doctor` CLI/integration tests (`tests/cli/doctor-*.test.ts`,
   `tests/doctor-*.test.ts`) pass unmodified.
4. **One concern per module.** Each extracted module registers exactly one
   doctor subcommand — or, for the shared notices module, one cohesive
   cross-cutting concern — carries a module-level doc comment stating its single
   responsibility, and moves its provenance comments (work-item ids) with the
   code.
5. **No cycles, narrow seams.** Extracted modules never import from
   `src/commands/doctor.ts`; the registrar passes a narrow typed context
   (`program`/`output`/`utils` and `dataPath` only where needed) so handlers do
   not depend on the full `PluginContext` surface.
6. **Line-count guard test (additive).** A new test asserts the doctor module
   family stays at or under 1,000 lines per file and fails when any module
   exceeds the ceiling (mirrors the `downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts`
   precedent from WL-0MVLIHWOY003IP5E — no existing test is touched).
7. **Documentation updated.** Any repository notes that describe the doctor
   command layout (e.g. `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CLI.md`, `docs/migrations.md`
   references) remain accurate, and the new module layout is stated in the
   top-of-file doc comment of `src/commands/doctor.ts`.
8. **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Relocate the existing action bodies and helpers into sibling
  modules, adjust imports and registration wiring; do not refactor their logic,
  rename flags, or reword user-facing output.
- **Entry point is fixed.** `src/commands/doctor.ts` must remain the dynamic
  import target in `src/command-registry.ts`; the split happens *behind* that
  path.
- **CLI-agnostic logic stays put.** `src/doctor/*.ts` holds CLI-independent
  validation logic (`status-stage-check`, `dependency-check`, `file-paths-check`,
  `hook-upgrade`, `foreign-items-check`, `audit-gaps-check`, `parent-check`,
  `podcast-scripts-check`, `fix`). It is consumed as-is; this item does not
  restructure it.
- **Serial, tree-green landing.** Extract the smallest subcommands first and the
  root validation/`--fix` action last, so every intermediate state builds and
  passes the suite.
- **No new runtime dependencies.** No changes to the doctor CLI contract, and no
  edits to the TUI or other commands.

## Existing state

`src/commands/doctor.ts` is 1,658 lines on today's `dev`. Inventory of logical
sections (line ranges from the current checkout):

| # | Section | Lines | Size |
|---|---------|-------|------|
| 1 | File header + imports | 1–30 | 30 |
| 2 | `DAY_MS` constant | 31 | 1 |
| 3 | `formatCacheBytes` helper | 33–46 | 14 |
| 4 | `DoctorOptions` type | 47–50 | 4 |
| 5 | `PendingUpgradeState` + `detectPendingUpgrades` | 51–92 | 42 |
| 6 | `buildPendingUpgradeFinding` | 93–129 | 37 |
| 7 | `printPendingUpgradeNotice` | 130–151 | 22 |
| 8 | `PendingCacheState` + `detectPendingCacheState` | 152–196 | 45 |
| 9 | `printPendingCacheNotice` | 197–207 | 11 |
| 10 | `register()` prologue + root `doctor` command definition | 208–217 | 10 |
| 11 | `doctor upgrade` action | 218–418 | 201 |
| 12 | `doctor stage-sync` action | 420–549 | 130 |
| 13 | `doctor prune` action | 551–649 | 99 |
| 14 | `doctor cache` action | 651–715 | 65 |
| 15 | `doctor foreign-items` action | 717–838 | 122 |
| 16 | `doctor audit-gaps` action | 840–877 | 38 |
| 17 | `doctor dangling-parents` action | 879–948 | 70 |
| 18 | `doctor priority` action | 950–1036 | 87 |
| 19 | `doctor file-paths` action | 1038–1150 | 113 |
| 20 | `doctor migrate` action | 1152–1271 | 120 |
| 21 | Root `doctor` action (findings aggregation, `--fix` interactive prompt, notices) | 1273–1657 | 385 |

Relevant structural facts discovered during intake:

- **Single consumer.** Only `src/command-registry.ts` imports the module
  (`doctor: () => import('./commands/doctor.js')`), and only for the default
  export. There is no cross-module use of helpers defined in the file, so
  extraction needs no public barrel beyond the unchanged default export.
- **Existing precedent for a nested sibling directory.** `src/sync.ts` (1,828
  lines, itself the subject of WL-0MVGKGMU400631VZ) already sits beside a
  `src/sync/` directory (`src/sync/merge-utils.ts`), so `src/commands/doctor.ts`
  + `src/commands/doctor/` follows an established repository shape.
- **CLI layer vs validation layer.** `src/doctor/` modules are pure,
  `PluginContext`-free validators; the monolith's bulk is CLI registration and
  output rendering. The split therefore belongs in the command layer, not in
  `src/doctor/`.
- **Test surface to keep green (unmodified).** 18 existing doctor suites —
  `tests/doctor-{dependency-check,file-paths,foreign-items-apply,foreign-items-check,hook-upgrade,podcast-scripts,retired-stage,status-stage}.test.ts`
  and `tests/cli/doctor-{audit-gaps,cache,foreign-items-apply,foreign-items-push,foreign-items,priority,prune,stage-sync,upgrade-notice,upgrade}.test.ts`.
  Source: `ls tests/doctor-*.test.ts tests/cli/doctor-*.test.ts`.

## Desired change

Reduce `src/commands/doctor.ts` to a thin registrar that wires the root
`doctor` command and delegates each subcommand to its own module under a new
`src/commands/doctor/` directory. Starting decomposition (boundaries are an
implementation decision, subject to the constraints above):

| New module | Responsibility | Approx. size |
|---|---|---|
| `src/commands/doctor.ts` | Registrar only: imports the per-subcommand registrars, registers the root `doctor` command definition, documents the module layout | ~120 |
| `src/commands/doctor/notices.ts` | Shared helpers: `DAY_MS`, `DoctorOptions`, `formatCacheBytes`, pending-upgrade detection/notice, pending-cache detection/notice | ~180 |
| `src/commands/doctor/upgrade.ts` | `doctor upgrade` (migrations + hook upgrade, dry-run/confirm) | ~205 |
| `src/commands/doctor/stage-sync.ts` | `doctor stage-sync` | ~135 |

## Summary

Add a `wl doctor prefix` subcommand that changes the configured project prefix in `.worklog/config.yaml` and renumbers every existing work item to the new prefix, preserving each item's suffix (e.g. `OSL-0MVK31VYQ007CN37` → `CC-0MVK31VYQ007CN37`). The flow must ask for confirmation before it changes anything, default to a read-only preview, and emit a machine-readable rename map.

## Motivation

Requested from the ContentCreator project (`/home/rgardler/projects/ContentCreator`), whose configured prefix is `OSL` while the project is now branded `CC`. 1207 work items carry the `OSL-` prefix, and `wl doctor foreign-items` correctly classifies any item whose prefix differs from `.worklog/config.yaml` as foreign — so editing the prefix by hand would make the whole backlog look foreign and break cross-project lookups.

## Scope (proposed)

- `wl doctor prefix` — read-only preview: current prefix, counts of items/comments/dependency edges/audit records, and sample renames.
- `wl doctor prefix --to <PREFIX>` — declare the target prefix (validated: non-empty, no `-`, ASCII alphanumeric).
- `wl doctor prefix --to <PREFIX> --confirm` — apply: rewrite the config prefix, then rewrite every ID-bearing record (`workitems.id`, parent references, dependency edges, comments' `workItemId`, audit results, waivers, and any other ID column), and write a rename map (`osl→cc` pairs) to `.worklog/prefix-rename-<timestamp>.json`.
- Confirmation gate: interactive run without `--confirm` prompts and requires an explicit `y`; a non-TTY run without `--confirm` aborts with no writes and a non-zero exit.
- Idempotent: re-running after a successful rename reports a no-op.
- `--json` output for scripting.
- Docs: `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md` and `CLI.md`.

## Acceptance criteria (draft)

- [ ] `wl doctor prefix` (preview) reports counts and sample renames and changes nothing; covered by unit and temp-store integration tests.
- [ ] `--confirm` rewrites every ID-bearing record (items, parents, dependency edges, comments, audit results, waivers) and writes the rename map.
- [ ] Confirmation gate: non-interactive without `--confirm` aborts with a non-zero exit and zero writes; interactive requires explicit `y`.
- [ ] Re-running after a successful rename is a no-op, and a mid-run failure leaves the store recoverable (transactional or a documented rollback).
- [ ] `wl doctor foreign-items` reports zero foreign items after a confirmed rename.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated (CLI.md, DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md, code comments).
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Out of scope

Rewriting ID references held outside the worklog store — code comments, docs, test fixtures, git commit messages, branch and worktree names. The requesting project owns that sweep and will use the rename map.

## Related

- Requested by work in the ContentCreator project (`discovered-from` recorded there).

# If Critical item is a child it should not show in top level herdr selection list (WL-0MVN4WESM007T4XI)

## Problem statement

The Herdr worklist renders critical-priority work items that have a `parentId` at the **top level** of the selection list, even when their parent is also listed — so a critical child appears twice: once as a standalone top-level row and once under its parent when expanded. The top level should contain only root items; a critical child must appear only as a child.

Confirmed live reproduction: `WL-0MVSNHCSM004JYEY` (critical, blocked, `intake_complete`, parent `WL-0MVSI1JMN002CGC0`) is a child of `WL-0MVSI1JMN002CGC0` (critical, in-progress). Both render at top level.

## Users

- **Producer / operator using the Herdr worklist** — browses the top-level selection list to choose what to work on next.
  - *As a producer, I want the top-level list to contain only root work items, so I am not shown the same unit of work twice and the list stays short enough to scan.*
- **Developer/agent triaging critical work** — needs release-blocking critical work to remain discoverable.
  - *As a triager, I want a critical child to be reachable from the top level via its parent, so hiding the duplicate row does not make the work invisible.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Top-level invariant**: the default Herdr worklist contains **no** item with a non-empty `parentId`, critical items included. Enforced on the merged set (browse feed + all mandatory subsets) for **both** fetch paths — the consolidated `wl worklist` bundle path (`assembleDefaultWorklist`) and the per-subset fallback — and by removing the `|| i.priority === 'critical'` exception from the root filter in `selectWorkItems`.
2. **Parent substitution preserves reachability**: when a critical child is dropped from the top level, its **root ancestor** (walking the `parentId` chain to the top-most non-child item) is included instead whenever that root is not already in the selected set. The substituted root joins the mandatory set (always shown, not subject to `browseItemCount`) and is sorted by its own priority/group. No badge, marker, or indicator is added to the substituted row.
3. **No regression for existing behaviour**:
   - non-critical children remain hidden from the top level exactly as today;
   - drill-down/expand still returns children unchanged (`fetchChildrenForItem` / `fetchChildrenForItems`, including critical children);
   - stage-filtered and priority-filtered views remain strictly root-only filters with **no** synthetic/substituted rows;
   - the CLI is unchanged for other consumers: `wl list --priority critical` still returns children (the ship critical-items gate must keep seeing them) and `wl worklist`'s `critical` subset keeps its current all-parent-levels query.
4. **Testing & validation**: unit tests cover the removed critical exception, the substitution rule (root ancestor promotion, parent already visible → no duplicate, parent in a non-critical group, count/mandatory interaction), and both fetch paths; the previously added critical-exception tests are updated/inverted. The full project test suite passes with the new changes.
5. **Documentation**: all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. At minimum: the root-filter comment in `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts`, the critical-subset note in `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` and `src/commands/worklist.ts`, and the Herdr worklist section of `packages/herdr/README.md`.

## Constraints

- **No new hot-path `wl` spawn.** Root-ancestor resolution must use the existing in-process SQLite fast path first (`withInProcessDb` / refresh scope `db.get`), with `wl show` only as a fail-open fallback. The refresh-spawn budget work (WL-0MVI0IT4S0070G78, WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG) must not regress.
- **No data mutation.** Substitution is display-layer only: never rewrite the parent's stored `priority`, `status`, or `stage`.
- **Keep the `wl worklist` critical subset query as-is** (all parent levels, one spawn). It doubles as the discovery feed that tells the Herdr layer which parents to surface; making it root-only would require a second query per refresh.
- **Ship-gate semantics untouched.** `wl list --priority critical --status open` (exit code 7 gate) and the downtime critical candidate path keep their current child-inclusive behaviour.
- Fail-open: if a parent cannot be resolved (missing/deleted), the child is simply not shown at top level — never crash the refresh, never fall back to rendering the child at top level.

## Existing state

- **Why the duplicate exists today.** Commit `cae8ea8a` ("fix: show child critical items in worklist selection list") deliberately reintroduced critical children into the top level: the critical subset query dropped `--root-only` and `selectWorkItems` gained the `|| i.priority === 'critical'` root-filter exception. Rationale: child criticals (e.g. untriaged `[test-failure]` items) were invisible in the worklist while the ship critical-items gate still blocked release on them (exit code 7).
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` — `selectWorkItems` root filter: `items.filter((i) => !i.parentId || i.priority === 'critical')`; `isMandatoryItem` treats any critical item as mandatory.
- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — `WORKLIST_LIST_SUBSET_QUERIES.critical = { priority: 'critical', status: ['open','in-progress','blocked','completed'] }` with **no** `rootOnly`, documented as "all parent levels: a critical child is as urgent as a critical root". `reviewQueue`, `inProgressRoots`, `blockedRoots` are all `rootOnly: true`.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `fetchMandatorySubsets` issues `wl list --priority critical --status open,in-progress,blocked,completed` (no `--root-only`); `assembleDefaultWorklist` merges bundle subsets with the browse feed then calls `selectWorkItems` + `regroupWorkItems`; the per-subset fallback mirrors this. `fetchItemsByStage` / `fetchItemsByPriority` already pass `--root-only`.
- `wl worklist` is consumed only by `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` (verified by search), so its payload shape is effectively a Herdr-internal contract.
- Current data: 174 critical items, 78 of them children — 77 of those are themselves `completed`/`done` (already filtered by the `stage !== 'done'` rule in `selectWorkItems`), leaving **one** live duplicate: `WL-0MVSNHCSM004JYEY`.
- The Pi TUI Worklog extension has no critical-subset or smart-selection code (removed by WL-0MSGI7PV9004UD0N), so no Pi-side change is needed.
- Parent rows already carry `childCount` (rendered as a `Children: N` metadata row and an expand icon), so a substituted parent is discoverable as a container.

## Desired change

1. **`packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts`** — root filter becomes `items.filter((i) => !i.parentId)` (no critical exception). Update the doc comment to state the invariant and the substitution contract.
2. **`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`** — add a display-layer substitution step shared by `assembleDefaultWorklist` and the per-subset fallback:
   - partition the critical subset into root criticals (kept) and critical children (dropped from the top level);
   - for each critical child, resolve its root ancestor by walking `parentId` upward;
   - for each resolved root not already present in the merged candidate set, add it to the **mandatory** set (so `browseItemCount` cannot cut it) before `selectWorkItems` runs;
   - resolve parents in-process first (`db.get` via the refresh scope / `withInProcessDb`), falling back to `wl show`; unresolvable parents are skipped (fail-open).
3. **`src/commands/worklist.ts`** — documentation-only update: state that the `critical` subset is intentionally all-parent-levels (discovery feed) and that the top-level-only invariant is enforced by the Herdr consumer.
4. **Tests** — invert/extend `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.test.ts` (child critical hidden; non-critical children still hidden) and add fetcher-level coverage for both paths in `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-worklist-bundle.test.ts` plus the per-subset fallback tests.
5. **Docs** — update `packages/herdr/README.md` (worklist/selection behaviour) and the affected code comments.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` — remove the critical exception from the root filter; document the invariant and substitution contract.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `assembleDefaultWorklist` + per-subset fallback: critical-child partition, root-ancestor resolution, mandatory-set injection; in-process-first parent lookup with `wl show` fail-open fallback.
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.test.ts` — invert the "shows child critical items at the top level" case; keep/extend non-critical child cases.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-worklist-bundle.test.ts` — bundle path: child critical not rendered at top level; parent substituted and mandatory.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.test.ts` (per-subset fallback coverage, whichever file currently exercises `fetchNextItems` without the bundle) — same assertions on the fallback path.
- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — comment/documentation update for the `critical` subset (no behaviour change).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — selection-list behaviour documentation.

## Related work

- **WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR** — *Hide child work items from top-level selection lists (Pi and Herdr)* (completed). Introduced the root-only invariant; its critical-related behaviour was later superseded by commit `cae8ea8a`. This item restores the invariant for critical items while keeping reachability via parent substitution.

B"** — substitute the parent; the child is never rendered at top level.

# Default downtime local preference should be remote-ok

**Headline:** Flip the downtime locality default from `local-only` to `remote-ok`
so unattended downtime work never queues the local slot the operator may need,
while `local-only` remains an explicit per-deployment opt-in.

## Problem statement

Downtime-dispatched panes default to `local-only`, so on a contended local slot
the proxy refuses the request immediately instead of falling back: the
unattended work simply does not run, even though remote capacity is available.
`local-only` is only *safe* when the operator has deliberately said "this work
must run here" — as a blanket default it strands work that could have run
remotely, and (see WL-0MVNUJG04005QL7G) cannot serve prompts above the local
provider's context ceiling at all.

## Users

- **Producer/operator running downtime dispatch.** Wants backlog work to keep
  moving unattended without competing for the local slot they need for
  interactive work.
- **Operator of a deliberately local-first deployment.** Wants the current
  fail-fast-local behaviour preserved, selected explicitly rather than by
  default.
- **Operator auditing dispatch behaviour.** Wants the route log to show
  `preference: remote-ok` on a default deployment, so "which default applied?"
  is evidence, not guesswork.

User stories:

- As a producer, I want downtime-dispatched panes to default to `remote-ok` so a
  contended local slot does not silently stall my backlog.
- As a producer running a local-first box, I want `downtimeLocalPreference:
  local-only` to keep today's behaviour exactly, with no other switch needed.
- As an operator, I want the route log of an unconfigured deployment to record
  `remote-ok`, so I can confirm the new default is live after deployment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Default constant.** `DOWNTIME_LOCAL_PREFERENCE` is `'remote-ok'` in
  `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.ts`; the module header documents
  `remote-ok` as the default and `local-only` as the per-deployment opt-in,
  cross-referencing this item and the superseded default in
  WL-0MVLJTV03000KIQZ.
- [ ] **Clamp.** `clampDowntimeLocalPreference` resolves every absent/invalid
  input (`undefined`, `null`, `''`, `'auto'`, `'both'`, `'Local-Only'`,
  `' remote-ok'`, `42`) to `remote-ok` via the constant, still passes
  `local-only` / `remote-ok` through verbatim, and never invents a value.
- [ ] **Settings default.** `defaultSettings.downtimeLocalPreference` is
  `'remote-ok'`, and `loadSettings` resolves a missing file, a file without the
  key, and an out-of-alphabet persisted value to `remote-ok`;
  `tests/herdr/settings.test.ts` (default + clamp cases) and
  `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.test.ts` are updated to pin it.
- [ ] **Dispatch paths inherit the default.** With no `downtimeLocalPreference`
  in `settings.json`, downtime backlog dispatch, own-backlog fallback,
  audit-batch continuation and scheduled-prompt dispatch all forward
  `remote-ok` to the pane (`--local-preference remote-ok` and
  `HERDR_LOCAL_PREFERENCE=remote-ok`), asserted by regression tests; the
  Worklog pi extension route-log test records `preference: "remote-ok"` for a
  `remote-ok` pane so the observable route log matches.
- [ ] **`local-only` stays selectable.** With `downtimeLocalPreference:
  'local-only'` persisted, every dispatch path still forwards `local-only`
  (existing C4-AC1 forwarding tests stay green) and nothing overrides it.
- [ ] **Documentation.** `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`,
  `packages/herdr/README.md` (setting list + per-turn local preference section)
  and `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` (where its prose implies a default)
  state `remote-ok` as the default, `local-only` as the opt-in, and make the
  scheduled/background inheritance explicit; related code comments in
  `settings.ts`, `downtime-worker.ts` and `local-preference.ts` are updated.
- [ ] **Testing/validation gate.** Changed-scope tests pass before commit and
  the full project test suite passes via `/skill:test` (no ad-hoc test runs).

## Constraints

- **Wire contract unchanged.** The request header alphabet stays exactly
  `local-only | remote-ok`; no new header, value or proxy (LP) change is in
  scope.
- **Fail-open preserved.** Unset/empty/invalid input still resolves to the
  default (now `remote-ok`), never throws and never invents a preference.
- **Optional internal field semantics unchanged.** `DowntimeWorkerConfig.config()
  .localPreference` stays optional: absent still means "no `--local-preference`,
  no `HERDR_LOCAL_PREFERENCE`, no route-log line" (byte-identical launch for
  hand-built/legacy configs). The new default reaches production panes through
  `loadSettings()` → plugin `config()`, which always supplies a value.
- **`BACKGROUND_LOCAL_PREFERENCE` stays separate** (`remote-ok`) and remains the
  fallback for callers that supply no knob. Scheduled prompts continue to take
  the knob when present — so an explicit `local-only` deployment also makes
  scheduled work local-only. That inheritance must be documented, not silently
  changed.
- **No priority-based rule here.** Priority → preference mapping is
  WL-0MVNUIW77000VYAX and layers on top of this default.
- **Interactive panes untouched.** No env var unless the operator exports
  `HERDR_LOCAL_PREFERENCE`; no new polling or logging behaviour.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.ts`: `DOWNTIME_LOCAL_PREFERENCE =
  'local-only'`, `BACKGROUND_LOCAL_PREFERENCE = 'remote-ok'`;
  `clampDowntimeLocalPreference()` returns `DOWNTIME_LOCAL_PREFERENCE` for
  anything not in the two-value alphabet.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts`: `defaultSettings.downtimeLocalPreference`
  uses the constant; `loadSettings()` clamps the persisted value through
  `clampDowntimeLocalPreference`, so absent/invalid already follows the
  constant (only the constant needs to change for AC1–AC3 to hold).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` forwards `s.downtimeLocalPreference` into the
  worker config and `s.downtimeLocalPreference`/`BACKGROUND_LOCAL_PREFERENCE`
  into the headless dispatcher.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` threads `localPreference` through
  `runDispatchTick` → `dispatchDowntimeWork` / `dispatchClaimedTier` →
  `spawnAgentPane` → `buildDowntimePaneArgs` (`--local-preference`) and
  `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` (`HERDR_LOCAL_PREFERENCE`); the scheduled-prompt
  path uses `opts.localPreference ?? BACKGROUND_LOCAL_PREFERENCE`.
- Tests currently pinning the old default: `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.test.ts`
  (`DOWNTIME_LOCAL_PREFERENCE === 'local-only'`) and `tests/herdr/settings.test.ts`
  (default and invalid-value clamp cases). Forwarding tests
  (`downtime-worker.reserve.test.ts`, `tests/herdr/send-to-pi.test.ts`,
  `coordination-dispatch.test.ts`, `downtime-worker.tiers.test.ts`) pass explicit
  values and should stay green.
- Documentation currently stating the default: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`
  (Policy knob paragraph), `packages/herdr/README.md` (setting list and the
  per-turn local preference section), `packages/tui/extensions/README.md`
  (policy-knob cross-reference).

## Desired change

1. Flip `DOWNTIME_LOCAL_PREFERENCE` to `'remote-ok'` and rewrite the module
   header + clamp doc comments so `local-only` reads as the explicit opt-in.
2. Update the `settings.ts` property comment and default wiring prose.
3. Update/add tests: new default (module + settings), absent-key and
   invalid-value clamping, unchanged verbatim pass-through, dispatch-path
   inheritance with no setting present, and the extension route-log
   `remote-ok` case.
4. Update the three documentation surfaces so the prose matches the code,
   including the explicit-`local-only` scheduled-prompt inheritance.
5. Record the supersession of the pinned C4-AC1 default on
   WL-0MVLJTV03000KIQZ (comment) so the changed decision is auditable.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.ts` — flip the default constant and
  rewrite the policy doc comments (default vs opt-in, supersession note).
- `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.test.ts` — pin `remote-ok` as the
  downtime default; keep clamp tests expressed relative to the constant.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — update the `downtimeLocalPreference`
  property comment; default already derives from the constant.
- `tests/herdr/settings.test.ts` — new default expectation and invalid-value
  clamp expectations (`'auto'`, `42` → `remote-ok`).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — comment prose for the
  `localPreference` field and dispatch paths (default now `remote-ok`).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.tiers.test.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.reserve.test.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts` — dispatch-path
  inheritance coverage (scheduled prompt, own-backlog fallback, audit-batch
  continuation) with no setting present.
- `packages/tui/extensions/local-preference/local-preference.test.ts` —
  route-log line with `preference: 'remote-ok'` (and header injection already
  covered for both values).
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — Policy knob paragraph (default, opt-in,
  scheduled inheritance).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — setting list entry and the per-turn local
  preference section.
- `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` — policy-knob prose if it implies a
  local-only default.

## Related work

- **WL-0MVLJTV03000KIQZ** (completed, *Per-turn local preference and route
  logging*) — introduced the knob, the wire contract and the `local-only`
  downtime default (C4-AC1) that this item supersedes; its default-pinning
  tests are updated here.
- **WL-0MVIKRFP0005JDL8** (completed) — parent downtime-dispatch epic whose
  AC4 slice C4 defined the locality policy.
- **WL-0MVNUIW77000VYAX** (*Dispatch low-priority work items with local-only
  preference*) — layers priority → preference on top of this default; its
  "explicit operator setting always overrides" rule stays intact.
- **WL-0MVNUJG04005QL7G** (*local-only requests over the local provider context
  limits are unprocessable*) — the context-ceiling limitation that makes a
  blanket `local-only` default unattractive; separate scope.
- **WL-0MVNUMI1B0021IGI** (open test-failure, `downtime-worker.pane-spawn.test.ts`)
  — unrelated failure in the same package; expect possible slot contention when
  running the herdr suites, not a dependency.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — cost/route shift.** `remote-ok` lets contended downtime work leave the
  box for a remote (possibly metered) provider. That is the intended trade
  ("never queue local capacity"), but it is a real change in spend profile;
  `local-only` stays the one-line opt-in and the route log makes the route
  visible. Document it, do not hide it.
- **Risk — silently superseding a pinned AC.** C4-AC1 (WL-0MVLJTV03000KIQZ)
  explicitly pinned `local-only`. Mitigation: the brief records the
  supersession, the code comment names it, and a comment is added to the
  predecessor item.
- **Risk — implicit-default migration.** Deployments that never wrote
  `downtimeLocalPreference` start going remote on contention. Intended, but it
  must be called out in the docs (and the release note handled by `/skill:ship`).
- **Risk — hidden default assumptions in tests.** Only
  `local-preference.test.ts` and `tests/herdr/settings.test.ts` were found
  asserting the old default; the changed-scope gate should confirm nothing else
  depends on it.
- **Assumption.** No proxy/LP change is required: the wire alphabet and headers
  are unchanged, only which value herdr prefers by default.
- **Assumption.** No settings migration is written: an explicit
  `'local-only'` value keeps working verbatim; only absent/invalid input
  resolves to the new default.
- **Scope-creep guard.** Priority-aware preference, context-ceiling routing and
  any "auto" heuristic stay in WL-0MVNUIW77000VYAX / WL-0MVNUJG04005QL7G — not
  here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive questions were required — the seed context (goal, exact file,
AC list and related items) was sufficient to draft this brief. Decisions that
would otherwise have been questions were resolved from repo evidence:

- Q: "Does `clampDowntimeLocalPreference` need a separate change, or does it
  follow the constant?" — Answer (research): follows the constant — it returns
  `DOWNTIME_LOCAL_PREFERENCE` for anything not in the alphabet
  (`packages/herdr/src/local-preference.ts`), so the single constant flip makes
  absent/invalid resolve to `remote-ok`. Source: repo inspection. Recorded as
  AC2 to keep the fail-open behaviour explicit.
- Q: "Do scheduled prompts and headless background dispatches need their own
  change?" — Answer (research): no — both already resolve to
  `BACKGROUND_LOCAL_PREFERENCE` (`'remote-ok'`) when no knob is supplied
  (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` `dispatchScheduledPrompt`,
  `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` `spawnBackgroundPi`), and with the new default
  the knob itself is `remote-ok`. Explicit `local-only` deployments inherit the
  knob, which must be documented (Constraint). Source: repo inspection.
- Q: "Which tests and docs assert the old default?" — Answer (research):
  `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.test.ts` and
  `tests/herdr/settings.test.ts` assert it; `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`,
  `packages/herdr/README.md` and `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` describe
  it. Source: `grep` over the main checkout.
- Q: "Does changing the default contradict completed work?" — Answer
  (research): yes — WL-0MVLJTV03000KIQZ C4-AC1 pinned `local-only`. This item
  supersedes that default; the supersession is recorded here and on the
  predecessor item rather than left implicit. Source: `wl show
  WL-0MVLJTV03000KIQZ`.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MVNUIW77000VYAX** – Dispatch low-priority work items with local-only preference (open)
- **WL-0MSL2ZQIF006QB4Q** – Herdr isIdleStatus: prefer local_active_query over global active_query for idle detection (completed)

- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: 0mvikrfp0005jdl8, 0mvljtv03000kiqz, absent, ac1, ac2 (+343 more)

## Problem

The test-run cache (`run_tests.py` + `test_cache.py`) can serve a **stale** result, and can also report **missing** for an entry that was just written. Both were observed in one session (WL-0MVP7QHUB003ZA2A). Root cause undiagnosed — the symptoms below contradict `compute_git_state`'s documented content-sensitive fingerprint, so the fingerprint itself may be captured at the wrong moment.

Discovered during WL-0MVP7QHUB003ZA2A (discovered-from).

## Symptom 1 — a stale GREEN was returned for a changed tree

While validating RED witnesses for the peer-offer cooldown work:

1. Production fix applied (5 dirty files) → `run_tests.py --scope changed --group herdr --json` → `Test Files 130 passed`.
2. Production changes reverted (`git checkout -- <3 prod files>`; 2 dirty test files) → the same command → **130 passed / 4007 tests**, i.e. the RED witnesses "passed" without the fix.
3. The same command again, after adding `console.log` diagnostics to those same two test files, **reused the same cache directory** (`metadata.json` `completed_at` unchanged) — a cache hit, despite the file contents having changed.
4. `--no-cache` produced the expected **4 failures**, confirming the RED witnesses were valid.

## Symptom 2 — `--summary` reports `missing` for an entry just stored

Immediately after `run_tests.py --scope full --json` finished green at HEAD (`Test Files 280 passed | 1 skipped`, `Tests 4102 passed | 5 skipped`, cache dir `ada07d39…` with `scope: full`, `test_type: full`, `exit_code: 0`), `run_tests.py --summary --suite all --json` (with and without `--scope full`) reported `{"scopes":{"all":"missing"}}`. The checkout was clean at the same HEAD; `compute_git_state()` returned `2838fdc3…` while the stored entry held `6155836a…` — so the entry was keyed on a *transient* dirty state that existed during the run (plugin/`wl`/`dist`/test-created files) and can never be queried again afterwards.

## Impact

- A RED/GREEN verification can be silently wrong — exactly the evidence an audit consumes.
- `implement.py finish`'s changed-scope gate can pass on a stale cached run.
- The audit's `query_cached()` fast path misses for the same reason, forcing an unnecessary full-suite re-execution (F3).
- Agents are likely to trust the green summary and never use `--no-cache`.

## Proposed direction (for intake)

- Make the fingerprint stable for the *state an operator/agent can reproduce*: exclude ignored/transient paths (`.worklog/`, `dist/`, test scratch dirs) from the dirty-path content hash, or snapshot the state before the run rather than after.
- Re-check the content-hash path for `--scope changed` runs (symptom 1) — the file list may be reused where the content hash is not.
- Surface `cached: true` prominently in human-readable output so a re-used result is never mistaken for a fresh one.
- Document/automate: verification runs that must prove RED/GREEN should use `--no-cache`.

## Acceptance criteria (draft)

- Editing only the contents of an already-modified file invalidates the cache entry for that scope/group.
- A run's entry is queryable by `--summary` immediately afterwards from a clean checkout at the same HEAD.
- A cached result is visibly marked as cached in non-JSON output.
- Regression tests: (a) two runs with a content-only change between them do not share a cache entry; (b) `--summary` finds the entry written by the preceding `--scope full` run.

# Downtime dispatcher starvation: three roots, three causes, one silent symptom

## Objective (headline)

Make downtime dispatch starvation **self-explanatory and non-permanent**: any root on this machine that has dispatchable work must either get dispatched, or report an exact machine-readable reason for not being dispatched — **never a bare `no-candidate`**.

## Problem statement

Diagnosed 2026-10-27T21:46–21:56Z: the downtime dispatcher reported `no-candidate` continuously while the GPU sat idle for ~7 minutes and three separate worklog roots each had dispatchable-looking work. Three **unrelated** faults collapsed into one **indistinguishable** log line:

| Root | Dispatchable in window | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| `AI_Hell` (30-item window) | 0 | every item held by the producer sentinel `assignee=Map` |
| `tce-the-rising` (25-item window) | 1 (`in_review` → audit) | audit tier structurally unreachable at the default prefill cap |
| `ContextHub` (30-item window) | 9 | zero coordination entries — no live herdr instance in the root |

Leader decision log for the whole period: `{"operation":"no-dispatch","reason":"idle-age-qualified",...}` then `{"operation":"no-dispatch","reason":"no-candidate","freeSlots":2,"totalSlots":2,...}`. The AI_Hell instance (`87558ae9`) checked in every 5 minutes for hours writing `workItemId: null` **with no reason**.

### Root causes

1. **Audit tier unreachable at the default prefill cap.** `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2` is evaluated against `effectiveFreeSlots = min(freeSlots, capacityBudget)` (`downtime-worker.orchestrator-dispatch.ts:529-534`). With the default serialised prefill gate (`local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1`, `in_flight: 0`, `freeSlots: 2`) → `capacityBudget=1` → `effectiveFreeSlots=1` → audit tier **never** eligible, so the `completed`/`in_review` queue never drains (AI_Hell: 1154 completed items; tce-the-rising: its single audit candidate has 0 dispatch-log entries).
2. **No attribution for empty offers or skipped tiers.** Check-ins log `workItemId: null` with no reason; the leader collapses every per-entry rejection into the terminal `no-candidate`; a tier skipped by the effective-budget clamp is invisible entirely.
3. **The `assignee` scheduling hold is invisible.** `assignee=Map` holds (AGENTS.md producer sentinel) are correctly refused by `classifyItemForDispatch` (WL-0MV85WCJJ0087VMP) — but an entire held window is indistinguishable from an empty or broken backlog.

## Users

- **Operator (primary)**: runs the local LLM fleet from herdr; the person who has to answer "why is nothing being dispatched?" — today it requires reading the dispatcher's source and re-running classification by hand. Wants starved roots to be self-diagnosing from the decision log and TUI.
- **Producer**: parks work with `assignee=Map` deliberately; wants the hold to be *surfaced* when it is the sole reason a root is idle, without the dispatcher ever auto-clearing it.
- **Audit-tier consumers**: `completed`/`in_review` items waiting on `/skill:audit` during downtime; currently starved under the default prefill configuration.

Example user stories:

- As an operator, I can read one line of `.worklog/downtime-coordination.log` and know whether a root is empty, fully held by `assignee=Map`, fully gated, or paced — so I don't have to re-run classification by hand.
- As a producer, I am warned in the TUI when my own `assignee` hold is the sole reason a root cannot dispatch — so I can distinguish "I parked this on purpose" from "the dispatcher is broken".
- As an operator running the default proxy config, I can rely on audits draining the review queue during idle time — so the queue doesn't grow unbounded.

## Acceptance criteria (epic)

- AC1: All three implementation children are `completed` and audited.
- AC2: A live verification on `AI_Hell`, `tce-the-rising` and `ContextHub` shows each root either dispatching or reporting an exact reason other than a bare `no-candidate`. **Accepted variance (producer decision, 2026-10-29):** `ContextHub` has no live downtime instance to observe — its `.worklog/downtime-coordination.log` was last written 2026-10-27T00:52:43Z and the root-registry cause is out of scope in `WL-0MVR8GDJ3008WY3Y` — so the recorded absence of an instance is accepted as that root's evidence instead of a forced dispatch (resolves OPEN QUESTION O2). The other two roots are verified live: `AI_Hell` dispatching (`AH-0MVSSSFXK005ZW8O` check-ins at 2026-10-29T00:21:57Z and 00:27:04Z) and `tce-the-rising` reporting `all-window-items-gated` (00:19:48Z / 00:24:57Z / 00:30:07Z).
- AC3: No regression in the existing `packages/herdr` downtime-worker suites; the prefill pacing contract (WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX) still holds for single-pane tiers.
- AC4: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` reflects the final behaviour, including an explicit reversal of the documented audit-skip-at-cap-1 rule.
- AC5: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (code comments, `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`; `CHANGELOG.md` is managed by the ship skill and excluded).
- AC6: Full project test suite passes with the new changes (enforced by the dev-push gate).

## Constraints

- Do **not** change the canonical ranking contract ("dispatcher == Herdr list head", WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2).
- Do **not** widen the dispatch window (WL-0MUNS8X97007C9H9 stays in force).
- Do **not** raise the prefill budget above what the proxy reports, and do not change the default `local_max_concurrent_prefills` unless intake finds the audit tier genuinely needs concurrent prefills (it does not — see Intake record).
- Do **not** auto-clear `assignee` holds (A3).
- Root registry / sweep of roots with no live instance is **out of scope** — filed as `WL-0MVR8GDJ3008WY3Y`.
- The `assignee`-hold surface must be strictly read-only and add no new `wl` subprocess spawns to the refresh path.
- Attribution tokens must be stable strings, additive-only (no change to dispatch decisions), and rate-limited like other decision-log entries.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator-dispatch.ts:529-534` — `effectiveFreeSlots = min(freeSlots, capacityBudget)`; the value flows to the audit tier check (`downtime-worker.dispatch.ts:337`, `downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts:468`).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.idle.ts:344` — `capacityBudget = inFlight >= cap ? 0 : cap - inFlight`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.constants.ts:84` — `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2` documented as a slot-count requirement.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts:957-968` — the silent `workItemId: null` check-in log line.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.gates.ts:499-503` + `downtime-worker.selection.ts:72-86` — the silent `assignee` hold refusal (`isAssigneeHeld`).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator-dispatch.ts:290` — `recordDecision` already supports `blocking: false` observations with rate limiting (the mechanism AC3 of child 2 needs).
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — currently *documents* the audit-skip-at-cap-1 rule as intended (must be reversed).

## Desired change

1. Evaluate the audit tier's free-slot minimum against the **slot budget** (`freeSlots`), never against the prefill-capacity budget; keep `effectiveFreeSlots` as the pacing input for single-pane tiers.
2. Record machine-readable empty-offer and tier-skip attribution in the decision log (`empty-window`, `all-window-items-held` + sentinel, `all-window-items-gated` + dominant gate, budget-skip tokens with the tier), plus per-entry rejection detail for coordination entries — additive only.
3. Surface an all-held dispatch window to the operator (TUI/worklist warning naming the sentinel values and count) with a shared classification helper used by both the TUI and the coordination-log token.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator-dispatch.ts` — effective-budget computation (`:529-534`) and decision-log writer (`recordDecision`, `:290`)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.idle.ts` — `evaluatePrefillPacing` / `capacityBudget` (`:344`)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.constants.ts` — `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS` (`:84`), decision-log constants
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.ts` — per-tier minimum checks (`:337`) and audit-tier selection
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` — dispatch-time rejection path and check-in empty-offer log (`:957-968`)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination.ts` — `computeMostImportantItem` (`:146`)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.gates.ts` — `classifyItemForDispatch` (`:499-503` assignee hold)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.selection.ts` — `isAssigneeHeld` (`:72-86`)
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` / `packages/herdr/src/dispatch-view.ts` — the TUI worklist surface for the all-held warning
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.*.test.ts` — pinning suites (audit-tier, gates, idle, coordination-dispatch, worklist)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — to be corrected/reversed + schema table additions
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — dispatch behaviour sections

## Related work

### Work items

- **WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX** (completed) — prefill pacing contract that created `effectiveFreeSlots`; must keep holding for single-pane tiers (epic AC3).
- **WL-0MVR8GDJ3008WY3Y** (open, out of scope) — root registry / sweep of roots with no live herdr instance; the `ContextHub` cause.

- **WL-0MTF0KLO10043YAN** / **WL-0MTII48OV008P2QU** (completed) — single machine-wide leader + global slot budget.
- **WL-0MV85WCJJ0087VMP** (completed) — assignee CAS claim; the refusal this epic surfaces.

- find-related additions: **WL-0MTRBOU0Y002M2CX**, **WL-0MUL2IZLF002S9X5** (worklist dispatch filter axis — surface precedent for child 3), **WL-0MSLUANM5004NNPU** (audit-tier re-dispatch exclusion tests).

### Docs

# Task: end-to-end verification — `local-preferred` deferral (busy slot → `Retry-After` → local completion, zero remote dispatch)

Parent: WL-0MVSI1JMN002CGC0 (Clients: adopt `local-preferred` preference and honour the deferral contract). This task covers that epic's **AC4**, which is deliberately separated from the two implementation children because it can only be proven after the retry-classification fix ships.

## Problem statement

The epic's two implementation children change what the clients *send* (`local-preferred` end-to-end). Nothing in them proves the behaviour the operator actually asked for: a `local-preferred` pane that finds the local slot busy is **deferred** — it receives a retryable 429 carrying `Retry-After`, waits, is admitted once capacity frees, and completes on the local model with **zero** remote dispatch. That chain also needs the pi client to stop treating the retryable 429 as terminal (WL-0MVSBF5XZ001H7V7), so it cannot be claimed by either child.

## Users and user stories

- **Operator who set `local-preferred`.** "I want proof that my local-first work actually stays local and resumes — not that it silently goes remote or abandons its turn after a 20-second wait."
- **Producer reviewing the epic.** "I want a single, auditable evidence trail (session ids, timestamps, proxy and route-log excerpts) so I can accept epic AC4 without re-running the experiment."
- **On-call engineer facing a deferred pane.** "I want the reproduction procedure documented, so the next time a pane sits idle waiting for capacity I can confirm it is deferral rather than a stall."

## Existing state (verified in this checkout)

- Deferral is refused today, not deferred: with `X-Local-Preference: local-only` the proxy returned a retryable 429 (`local_admission_reject`, `retry_after: 15`, `Retry-After: 15`) and the pi client treated it as terminal, abandoning the turn (observed 2026-10-28, session `herdr-1793202136-1305210-5578`; tracked as WL-0MVSBF5XZ001H7V7).
- Evidence artefacts that already exist: the extension writes one bounded JSONL line per provider response to `<worklog-root>/.worklog/local-route.log` with `at`, `sessionId`, `preference`, `route`, `fallbackReason`, `model`, `ticket` (WL-0MVLJTV03000KIQZ); the proxy reports `X-Local-Route` / `X-Local-Fallback-Reason`; herdr records the dispatch marker (including `localPreference` and `localPreferenceReason`). The proxy-side log path is host-specific and must be resolved at run time — it does **not** exist at `/var/log/llama-proxy/` on every host.
- Dispatch/reproduction entry points: `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh --local-preference <value>` for a hand-launched pane, and the downtime worker for a dispatched pane. Local-slot saturation is driven by concurrent local requests (the proxy's admission guard projects an ETA against a fixed budget).

## Desired change

- Produce and record the end-to-end evidence on this work item, then leave it ready for review. No production behaviour change is expected; if the evidence contradicts the contract, that mismatch becomes a **new** blocking bug work item (created as a child of the epic or a `discovered-from:<this-id>` item) rather than an inline fix.
- Document the reproduction procedure (how to saturate the local slot, which logs to read, what a deferred-then-admitted sequence looks like) so the evidence can be re-derived.

## Constraints and decisions

- **Blocked-by WL-0MVSBF5XZ001H7V7.** Recorded as a `dep` edge (this item depends on that fix); the verification must not be attempted against a client that still classifies the retryable 429 as terminal, because a failure would be indistinguishable from the known bug.
- **No fabricated evidence.** Every claim must cite a concrete artefact: proxy log line, route-log JSONL line, or dispatch marker, with session id + timestamp. Synthetic fixtures may illustrate the expected shape but never substitute for a live observation.
- **Bounded, redacted excerpts.** Log excerpts recorded on the work item are trimmed to the relevant lines and must not include prompts, headers carrying credentials or full request bodies.
- **Evidence lives on the work item** (comments), not in a committed log file — `.worklog/local-route.log` is runtime state. If a doc change is justified it is limited to the deferral/reproduction paragraph in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.
- **Zero remote dispatch is a hard criterion:** any `remote:*` route entry, or any fallback reason, for the verified pane means AC2 fails even if the turn eventually succeeded locally.
- Out of scope: changing the proxy's deferral policy (llm epic LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY), the client retry semantics themselves (WL-0MVSBF5XZ001H7V7), and herdr/extension value plumbing (WL-0MVSI1RX2005O9NE, WL-0MVSI1S5P003UAMB).

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Preconditions verified.** The item records that WL-0MVSBF5XZ001H7V7 is completed (its dep edge resolved) and that both plumbing children are in `in_review`/completed, together with the herdr and proxy versions used.
- **AC2 — Deferral observed.** A live evidence trail shows a `local-preferred` pane whose request was deferred by the proxy: the retryable 429 (`local_admission_reject` / `local admission refused`, `retryable: true`, `Retry-After`/`retry_after`) plus the client honouring the hint (a retry no earlier than the advertised delay) instead of abandoning the turn.
- **AC3 — Local completion, zero remote.** The same pane's turn completes on the local model, and its `.worklog/local-route.log` entries for that session show `preference: local-preferred` with a local route and **no** `remote:*` route or fallback reason.
- **AC4 — Auditable evidence recorded.** The work item carries the session id(s), timestamps, the proxy log excerpt and the route-log excerpt (bounded and redacted), and the dispatch marker's `localPreference`/`localPreferenceReason` for the pane.
- **AC5 — Reproduction documented.** The procedure to saturate the local slot and read the evidence is documented (in the item comment, and in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` if it is reusable operator guidance).
- **AC6 — Tests.** Any new deterministic test or fixture added for this work passes, and the extension/herdr suites covering the route log remain green; if no test is added, the item states why live evidence is the only viable proof.
- **AC7 — Docs.** **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
- **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**
- **AC9 — Epic AC4 traceability.** Deferral is end-to-end: a `local-preferred` pane hitting a busy local slot retries per `Retry-After` and completes locally, with zero remote dispatch.
- **AC10 — Epic AC5 gate.** AC4 is not claimed until WL-0MVSBF5XZ001H7V7 (pi client treats the retryable 429 as terminal) ships; the dependency is recorded on this item's `dep` edge and in the epic's final comment.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — deferral/reproduction guidance (only if reusable operator guidance is warranted).
- `.worklog/local-route.log` — read-only evidence source (not committed).
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` — hand-launch entry point used to drive the reproduction.
- `packages/tui/extensions/local-preference/local-preference.ts` — route-log fields the evidence is read from (no change expected).
- Host proxy log — resolved at run time (path is deployment-specific; do not hard-code `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log`).

## Related work

- Parent epic WL-0MVSI1JMN002CGC0 (AC4 is the criterion this task exists to satisfy).
- **Blocking:** WL-0MVSBF5XZ001H7V7 — pi client currently treats the retryable local-admission 429 as terminal.
- Sibling children: WL-0MVSI1RX2005O9NE (herdr plumbing) and WL-0MVSI1S5P003UAMB (extension emits the header).
- Proxy-side contract, llm store: epic LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY; deferral/chain selection LP-0MVSHXTLS000VMLE; capacity verdict LP-0MVSHX47F003XEIZ; alias parser LP-0MVSHWYVE005MS16.
- Precedent: WL-0MVLJTV03000KIQZ (route log introduced), WL-0MVIKRFP0005JDL8 (reservation + per-turn preference), WL-0MU9Z7L8X00117BI (the existing `Retry-After` honouring the deferral reuses).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — the verification window never appears naturally.** Saturation depends on real concurrent local traffic. *Mitigation:* drive it deterministically by issuing concurrent saturating local requests (documented in AC5) rather than waiting for an organic busy period.
- **Risk — evidence is ambiguous.** A turn that retried and then went remote would look "successful" but fail AC3. Mitigated by making the zero-remote criterion explicit and by citing the route log per session.
- **Risk — the proxy contract differs from the assumed shape** (`retryable: true` + `Retry-After`). If the live response shape differs, AC2 is re-scoped against the observed contract and the discrepancy is filed as a bug against the episode's proxy child rather than silently accepted.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Improving the recovery loop or adding new observability during verification is out of scope; findings become separate work items.
- **Assumption:** this host can reach the local proxy and read its log (path resolved at run time); if not, the verification is recorded as **blocked on environment access** with an explicit OPEN QUESTION rather than being marked complete.
- **Assumption:** route-log entries are keyed by pi session id, which is enough to attribute every request of the verified pane.

## Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

- Q: Why is epic AC4 not folded into one of the two implementation children?
  — Answer (agent): it depends on WL-0MVSBF5XZ001H7V7 (client retry classification), which is outside both children's scope; keeping it separate lets the two plumbing children ship and close while AC4 stays honestly unclaimed. Source: WL-0MVSI1JMN002CGC0 AC4 text.
- Q: Should the evidence be committed to the repository?
  — Answer (agent): no — `.worklog/local-route.log` is bounded runtime state and may contain session metadata; the evidence is recorded as bounded, redacted excerpts in work-item comments. Source: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (route-log description).
- Q: Is a live run available in this environment right now?
  — Answer: unknown/not yet — `OPEN QUESTION` pending the dep edge resolving and the proxy log path being confirmed on this host. Not blocking this intake; it is AC1 of the task itself.
